summary: Help requested: staged reversion simulation and runbook for mixed quantization + prefix-caching changes
description:
Issue summary:
CodexHealth applied an optimization bundle (quant_profile=int4-aggressive, kv_prefetch=enabled, batch_policy=auto_coalesce with max_batch_tokens=4096) to their Dedicated pool last night. After the change they observed intermittent latency spikes (95th percentile token time up ~2.8x) and increased tail error rates for streaming requests. They want guidance to: (1) safely simulate a staged reversion in a non-production snapshot; (2) a concise runbook to perform a staged reversion in prod with minimal user-impact; (3) verification checks to confirm the reversion success.

Impact:
- Customer-facing features degrade: chat latency and streaming disconnects affecting ~7% of requests during peak hours.
- Business impact: degraded SLAs for certain enterprise customers; CodexHealth flagged incident to their SREs.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated) running on us-west-2 GPUs.
- Service: text-generation and streaming APIs with model routing to redwood-v1-large (primary) and open-llama-30b (fallback).
- Recent optimizer flags deployed via console feature-flags at 2026-03-11 23:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Send 1:1 chat streaming workload with average prompt length 220 tokens and burst concurrency ~70.
2) Use model redwood-v1-large pinned to v1.4-opt.
3) Observe 95th percentile token latency and streaming disconnect rate over 30 minutes.

Observed behavior:
- 95th percentile token generation time jumped from ~45ms to ~125ms.
- Streaming disconnects increased to 0.8% from baseline 0.05%.
- Trial reverting only batch_policy to conservative reduced latency but did not fully restore baseline.

Expected behavior:
- Optimizer changes should improve throughput/cost without materially increasing tail latency or streaming errors.

Logs / artifacts attached:
- Perf dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/opt/1234-codex-health (customer supplied snapshot).
- Error traces: s3://redwood-support/codexhealth/streams/errors_20260312.log
- Feature flag change history: console audit https://console.redwood.ai/audit/flags/67

Request:
- Provide a reproducible simulation recipe that the customer can run against a recent snapshot of their traffic (or an internal sim we can run) to validate the effect of each optimization independently (quant, kv-prefetch, batching coalescing).
- Provide a short, low-risk staged reversion runbook for prod which includes: pre-checks, stepwise toggles, quick verification queries, fallback triggers, and communication templates for the customer to notify their users.

Caveats:
- Customer prefers minimal downtime; they will accept brief token-level throttling windows if necessary.
- Their dedicated pool has no immediate capacity to rollback to older hardware images; solution should focus on software-level toggles and traffic routing where possible.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:14 - Support (Asha): Ticket created after receiving escalation from CodexHealth SRE. Initial hypothesis: mixed aggressive quant + kv-prefetch interacts poorly with continuous batching in their long-context workload.
2026-03-12 11:02 - Eng (Miguel): Assigned for investigation. Will reproduce using customer's load profile in staging snapshot. Requested the customer's sim corpus and the exact feature-flag dump.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Support (Asha): CodexHealth provided sim corpus (s3://codexhealth-sim/20260311) and flag dump. Noted they previously tested int8 and saw no regressions.

2026-03-13 02:10 - Eng (Miguel): Ran isolated sims in internal staging: toggled quant_profile only => marginal latency increase (~1.1x). Toggled kv_prefetch only => 95p latency increase (~2.2x) under bursty long-context traffic. Toggled batch_policy to conservative => reduced latency close to baseline but cost increased. Conclusion: kv_prefetch + auto_coalesce introduces reordering/lock contention under this workload.

2026-03-13 09:55 - SRE (Priya Kapoor): Noted autoscaler kept GPU utilization high; suggested adding a staged traffic-splitting plan (route 20% to baseline variant) to validate in prod before full revert.

2026-03-13 14:20 - Support (Asha): Drafted runbook v0.1 for Miguel to review. Includes stepwise toggles: 1) enable conservative batching, 2) disable kv_prefetch, 3) switch quant_profile to int8-safety, 4) monitor 95p and streaming error. Each step holds for 10 minutes with rollback trigger thresholds.

2026-03-14 08:05 - Eng (Miguel): Reviewed runbook and added simulation commands and safe-guard checks (heatmap of kv-cache hit ratios, rpc queue length, gpu kernel stalls). Also added Canary split configuration to route 10/30/60/100 percent over 15 minute ramps.

2026-03-14 11:30 - Customer (CodexHealth - SRE lead): Approved staged reversion plan; requested we run the initial canary ramp tomorrow during low-traffic window and provide a communication template for the feature flags timeline.
resolution: Workaround and staged reversion plan provided: disable kv_prefetch on customer pool and set batch_policy to conservative via console feature flags. Canary traffic split recommended (10%->30%->60%->100%). Pending execution by customer SRE for production ramp. Engineering created a follow-up internal task to add an assertion to scheduler to limit prefetch concurrency for long-context sessions.
resolution_notes:
- Reproduction in staging showed kv_prefetch as the dominant contributor to tail latency under long-context, high-concurrency workloads.
- Short-term fix: disable kv_prefetch and use conservative batching.
- Medium-term: add scheduler guardrails limiting prefetch concurrency and make quant_profile recommendations per workload shape.
- Follow-up PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/499 (prefetch-concurrency-guard).
- Customer agreed to run canary ramp on 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC; Support will monitor metrics and be on-call for rollback.
